facts.fact: Ponni is an old fishwife of Nellimala, now sleeping in Kesu's cattle shed in the pass village; she ran with baby Indu in her arm for the first bend of the goat path before Ammini took her.
facts.why: needed because the beat names the woman and her link to Neela's childhood.

facts.fact: Neela's mother Ammini was a net-mender of Nellimala who tied the fisherman's double hitch and went up the goat path after her daughter and did not come down.
facts.why: needed because the beat gives Neela's mother's name and fate.

facts.fact: At the second harvest two Thurai boats crossed the bar at slack water without a pilot, 'as if expected'. Men in grey waited at the top of the goat path with a flat cart whose tailboard bore a small, new yellow bird; one of them counted the youngest children as they were lifted onto it.
facts.why: needed because the beat specifies the harvest account, the grey men and the bird on the cart (clues C01, C07).

facts.fact: Neela remembers, at twelve or thirteen, seeing Chathu rewrite Kirri's rat-eaten page in resin-ink in his room, saying 'A master who saw you turn can always write you again.'
facts.why: needed because the beat requires the Chathu memory triggered by Kuttu's gnawed intake roll.

facts.fact: Devan tells Neela the grey-cloaked household man who recruited Muthu comes to mind, but notes the Kettamala garrison and many hill villagers also wear grey, and says he will not build on it.
facts.why: needed because the beat has him raise the grey-cloak link without pushing a conclusion.

facts.fact: The Company's members read their own intake rolls by the fire at the lightning boulder the night before the Kodiyur party leaves at first light.
facts.why: needed to set the scene for the intake-roll memory.
